easy.def: Of that kind, or so much.
examples: It was such a fun day.
I have never seen such a big dog.
She is such a good friend.

more.def: So great, or of the kind that was just named.
examples: It was such a beautiful day that we ate lunch outside.
Animals such as bears and frogs sleep through the winter.
I had never seen such a huge pumpkin.

easy.def: Very fast, with no warning.
examples: Suddenly it rained.
The lights suddenly went out.
A bird suddenly flew up.

more.def: Quickly and without warning.
examples: The sky suddenly turned dark.
A deer suddenly jumped across the road.
Suddenly the music stopped.

easy.def: To say an idea for someone to think about.
examples: I suggest we play tag.
She suggested a walk.
He suggests a movie.

more.def: To offer an idea or plan for others to think about.
examples: I suggest we take the bus.
She suggested a game of tag.
The teacher suggested reading a chapter each night.

easy.def: A jacket and pants that match.
examples: Dad wore a suit.
The man's suit is gray.
He put on a suit.

more.def: A jacket and pants, or a jacket and skirt, made of the same cloth and worn together.
examples: He wore a gray suit to the meeting.
Her new suit has a blue jacket and skirt.
The tailor made a suit for the wedding.

easy.def: Clothing for one special use.
examples: I wear a suit to swim.
The diver wore a suit.
Astronauts wear a space suit.

more.def: Clothing worn for a special activity.
examples: The astronaut put on a space suit.
She packed her swimming suit.
The firefighter's suit protects her from heat.

easy.def: To look good on someone.
examples: Blue suits you.
That hat suits her.
The color suits him.

more.def: To look good on a person, or to be right for them.
examples: That green color really suits you.
A warm coat suits this weather.
The plan suits everyone.

easy.def: The hot season between spring and fall.
examples: We swim in summer.
Summer is hot.
School is out for the summer.

more.def: The warmest season of the year, between spring and fall.
examples: We go camping every summer.
Fireflies glow in the summer evenings.
In summer, the days are long and sunny.

easy.def: The bright star that gives us light and heat.
examples: The sun is hot.
The sun came up.
We sit in the sun.

more.def: The star at the center of our solar system, which gives Earth light and heat.
examples: The Earth travels around the sun.
The sun rises in the east.
Plants need the sun to grow.

easy.def: Warm light from the sky.
examples: Cats like to nap in the sun.
Sit in the sun.
We played in the sun all day.

more.def: The warm light that shines down from the sky during the day.
examples: We sat in the sun to dry off.
Flowers turn toward the sun.
The sun felt warm on my face.

easy.def: To hold something up.
examples: Pillars support the roof.
The shelf supports the books.
A strong beam supports the roof.

more.def: To hold something up so it does not fall.
examples: Strong pillars support the porch roof.
The shelf supports the heavy books.
A crutch supports his leg.

easy.def: To help and cheer someone on.
examples: I support my team.
We support our friend.
Fans support the team.

more.def: To help someone or encourage them by showing you care.
examples: Her friends came to support her at the game.
Parents support their children.
We support our local library.

easy.def: Help.
examples: I need your support.
Thanks for the support.
The team has support from fans.

more.def: Help or encouragement that you give someone.
examples: Thank you for your support during the game.
He had support from his family.
The team has strong support from fans.

easy.def: To think something is likely.
examples: I suppose it will rain.
I suppose you are hungry.
We suppose she forgot.

more.def: To think that something is probably true, without being sure.
examples: I suppose the store is closed because it is a holiday.
I suppose we could take the bus instead.
What do you suppose made that noise?

easy.def: Expected or told to do something.
examples: I am supposed to go.
You are supposed to wait.
She is supposed to call.

more.def: Expected or required to do something, according to a plan or a rule.
examples: We are supposed to leave at eight o'clock.
You are supposed to wash your hands before you eat.
The bus was supposed to arrive ten minutes ago.

easy.def: Knowing that it is true.
examples: I am sure it is mine.
Are you sure?
She is sure she can do it.

more.def: Having no doubt about something, or certain to happen.
examples: I am sure that I left my backpack by the door.
Are you sure this is the right way to the beach?
Our team is sure to win after practicing so hard.

easy.def: Something you did not know would happen.
examples: The party was a surprise!
I have a surprise for you!
What a nice surprise to see you!

more.def: Something that happens that you did not expect.
examples: It was a nice surprise to find a letter in the mailbox.
To my surprise, the cat liked the bath.
The ending of the book was a complete surprise.

easy.def: Feeling that something happened that you did not expect.
examples: I was surprised by the gift.
She looked surprised.
He was surprised to see snow.

more.def: Feeling or showing that something unexpected has happened.
examples: I was surprised to see my cousin at the door.
She looked surprised when the lights came on.
We were surprised by the sudden storm.

easy.def: To stay alive.
examples: Plants need water to survive.
Fish can not survive out of water.
The plant survived the cold.

more.def: To stay alive, especially through something hard or dangerous.
examples: Camels can survive for days without drinking water.
The sailors survived the storm.
Few plants can survive in such dry soil.

easy.def: A person who may have done something wrong.
examples: The police questioned the suspect.
The detective found a suspect.
The suspect ran away.

more.def: A person who is thought to have done a crime.
examples: The detective questioned the suspect.
The police looked for the suspect.
No suspect has been found.

easy.def: To think something is true without being sure.
examples: I suspect it will rain.
She suspects her brother ate it.
He suspected a trick.

more.def: To think that something is probably true, or that someone did something, without being sure.
examples: I suspect the cat ate the fish.
She suspected a surprise party.
He suspected the story was a joke.
